title: Three Seasons and One Short Whistle
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：sport　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sport 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the coach ① loved the sport that no player in the field would have counted, and he said the loving was the whole of the season. The ② sport, meaning the game itself and not the whistle, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; a sport, he said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ sport in that field had the same short whistle beside it, and the ④ sport at the far stand, meaning the goal they kept for the children to cheer and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sport, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the coach said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sport was the whole of the matter, meaning the spirit and not the game. The ⑥ sport, meaning the spirit and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; sport, he said, is either something you love or the only word that means both a game and a spirit. He said the spirit is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ sport had become a line in a record, and the record had become an argument about the short whistle. The ⑧ sport of the whole thing, the coach wrote in April, was one field and three seasons of counting; sport, he said, is either the goal at the far stand or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sport I remember is the game counted in the record, which closed in 1959 and is still counted as the quietest in the field. A ⑩ sport, my mother said in 1961, is the only game that improves by being counted; every sport, she said, is a spirit that has agreed to look like a game. She said the spirit was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 运动（指球场里每一项旁边的那一项）
B. n. 运动（指那项运动本身，与小小的哨子相对）
C. 固定搭配：love the sport 爱好这一项运动
D. n. 运动（指留给孩子们喊的那一个）
E. n. 运动之事（抽象总称，指一处球场的运动之事）
F. n. 运动（指赛事记录里写到、被清点的那一项）
G. n. 运动、心气（指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 心气（抽象总称，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: loved the sport that no player in the field would have counted
The sport, meaning the game itself and not the whistle
the sport at the far stand

answers.why: love the sport 意为“爱好这一项运动”，1952 年那位教练把球场里没有一位队员肯清点的一项运动做了一遍。
sport 意为“运动”，指那项运动本身而不是小小的哨子，它经过了三个赛季而在簿子上没有被清点。
sport 意为“运动”，指球场里每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一只小小的哨子。
sport 意为“运动”，指最远那面看台的留给孩子们喊的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sport 意为“运动、心气”，指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这项心气就是那件事的全部。
sport 意为“心气”，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西而不是那项运动，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sport 意为“运动”，指赛事记录里写到、被清点的那一项，到 1957 年这一项成了赛事记录里的一行。
sport 意为“运动之事”，教练四月写道，整件事的运动之事是一处球场和三个赛季的清点。
sport 意为“运动”，我记得的是赛事记录里清点过的那一项，1959 年打完了，至今仍被说成球场里最安静的一项。
sport 为抽象总称，母亲 1961 年说，运动是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的运动。
